```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

from pathlib import Path
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import statsmodels.api as sm
from IPython.display import display
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# ── paths ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
BASE        = Path(".")
DATA_DIR    = BASE / "data"
OUTPUT_DIR  = BASE / "output"
OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

FACTOR_FILE    = DATA_DIR / "F-F_Research_Data_Factors_daily.csv"
PORTFOLIO_FILE = DATA_DIR / "6_Portfolios_2x3_Daily.csv"

PORTFOLIO_COLS = ["SMALL LoBM","ME1 BM2","SMALL HiBM",
                  "BIG LoBM",  "ME2 BM2", "BIG HiBM"]
FACTOR_COLS    = ["MKT","SMB","HML"]
PALETTE        = ["#2f6f73","#8a5a44","#6f5aa8","#b5722d","#4a7c4e","#a84c4c"]

sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", font="DejaVu Sans")

# ── matplotlib: let Quarto control figure size via fig-width/fig-height ────
# We pass figsize=(W, H) matching the Quarto defaults so savefig is consistent
PDF_W, PDF_H   = 6, 3.8
HTML_W, HTML_H = 7, 4.5

# ── data loading ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def read_first_panel(path):
    df = pd.read_csv(path)
    first_blank = df["TIME"].isna().idxmax() if df["TIME"].isna().any() else len(df)
    return df.iloc[:first_blank].copy()

def load_factors():
    ff = read_first_panel(FACTOR_FILE)
    ff = ff.rename(columns={"TIME":"Date","Mkt-RF":"MKT","SMB":"SMB",
                             "HML":"HML","RF":"RF"})
    ff[FACTOR_COLS+["RF"]] = ff[FACTOR_COLS+["RF"]].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    ff = ff.dropna(subset=["Date"]+FACTOR_COLS+["RF"])
    ff["Date"] = pd.to_datetime(ff["Date"], format="%Y%m%d")
    return ff.set_index("Date")

def load_portfolios():
    port = read_first_panel(PORTFOLIO_FILE)
    port = port.rename(columns={"TIME":"Date"})
    port[PORTFOLIO_COLS] = port[PORTFOLIO_COLS].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    port = port.dropna(subset=["Date"]+PORTFOLIO_COLS)
    port["Date"] = pd.to_datetime(port["Date"], format="%Y%m%d")
    return port.set_index("Date")

def prepare_data():
    ff   = load_factors()
    port = load_portfolios()
    data = port.merge(ff, left_index=True, right_index=True, how="inner")
    for col in PORTFOLIO_COLS:
        data[f"{col}_excess"] = data[col] - data["RF"]
    return data

def run_ff3(data):
    X = sm.add_constant(data[FACTOR_COLS])
    rows, models = [], {}
    for col in PORTFOLIO_COLS:
        m = sm.OLS(data[f"{col}_excess"], X).fit(cov_type="HAC",
                                                  cov_kwds={"maxlags":5})
        models[col] = m
        rows.append({
            "Portfolio" : col,
            "Alpha"     : m.params["const"],
            "t(Alpha)"  : m.tvalues["const"],
            "β(MKT)"    : m.params["MKT"],
            "t(MKT)"    : m.tvalues["MKT"],
            "β(SMB)"    : m.params["SMB"],
            "t(SMB)"    : m.tvalues["SMB"],
            "β(HML)"    : m.params["HML"],
            "t(HML)"    : m.tvalues["HML"],
            "R²"        : m.rsquared,
            "Adj. R²"   : m.rsquared_adj,
            "N"         : int(m.nobs),
        })
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("Portfolio"), models

data           = prepare_data()
reg_table, _   = run_ff3(data)
excess_cols    = [f"{col}_excess" for col in PORTFOLIO_COLS]
START          = data.index.min().strftime("%B %d, %Y")
END            = data.index.max().strftime("%B %d, %Y")
N_OBS          = len(data)
```

# Introduction

This report replicates the **Fama-French three-factor (FF3) model** using
daily data from Kenneth French's data library. The six test portfolios are
formed on the two-way sort of **size** (market equity, ME) and
**book-to-market ratio** (BM), yielding 2 × 3 = 6 portfolios.

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| MKT    | Excess market return ($R_m - R_f$) |
| SMB    | Small-Minus-Big (size factor) |
| HML    | High-Minus-Low (value factor) |

The regression specification for portfolio $i$ is:

$$
R_{i,t} - R_{f,t} = \alpha_i
  + \beta_i^{\text{MKT}}\,\text{MKT}_t
  + \beta_i^{\text{SMB}}\,\text{SMB}_t
  + \beta_i^{\text{HML}}\,\text{HML}_t + \varepsilon_{i,t}
$$

Standard errors are **Newey-West** adjusted (5 lags).

# Factor Summary Statistics

```{python}
#| label: tbl-factor-stats
#| tbl-cap: "Descriptive statistics for Fama-French daily factors (% per day)."

fstats = data[FACTOR_COLS].agg(["mean","std","min","max"])
fstats.loc["Skewness"] = data[FACTOR_COLS].skew()
fstats.loc["Kurtosis"] = data[FACTOR_COLS].kurt()
fstats.loc["t-stat"]   = (fstats.loc["mean"] / fstats.loc["std"] * np.sqrt(N_OBS))
fstats.index = ["Mean","Std Dev","Min","Max","Skewness","Kurtosis","t-stat"]
display(fstats.round(4))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-factor-ts
#| fig-cap: "Daily time series of the three Fama-French factors."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5.5

fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=(7, 5.5), sharex=True)
colors = ["#2f6f73","#8a5a44","#6f5aa8"]
labels = ["MKT — Market excess return",
          "SMB — Small Minus Big",
          "HML — High Minus Low"]

for ax, factor, color, lbl in zip(axes, FACTOR_COLS, colors, labels):
    ax.plot(data.index, data[factor], color=color, linewidth=0.5, alpha=0.85)
    ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.6, linestyle="--")
    ax.set_ylabel(f"{factor} (%)", fontsize=9)
    ax.set_title(lbl, fontsize=9, pad=2)

axes[-1].set_xlabel("Date", fontsize=9)
fig.suptitle("Daily Fama-French Three Factors", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(OUTPUT_DIR/"figure_factor_timeseries.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()
```

# Portfolio Excess Return Statistics

```{python}
#| label: tbl-port-stats
#| tbl-cap: "Descriptive statistics for 6 portfolio daily excess returns (% per day)."

pstats = data[excess_cols].agg(["mean","std","min","max"]).T
pstats.index = PORTFOLIO_COLS
pstats.columns = ["Mean","Std Dev","Min","Max"]
pstats["Sharpe (ann.)"] = (pstats["Mean"] / pstats["Std Dev"]) * np.sqrt(252)
pstats["t-stat"]        = pstats["Mean"] / pstats["Std Dev"] * np.sqrt(N_OBS)
display(pstats.round(4))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-cumret
#| fig-cap: "Cumulative excess returns of the six size-BM portfolios (log scale)."
#| fig-width: 7

cumulative.columns = PORTFOLIO_COLS

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5))

    ax.plot(cumulative.index, cumulative[col],
            linewidth=1.1, label=col, color=color)

ax.set_title("Cumulative Excess Returns — 6 Size × BM Portfolios",
             fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
ax.set_xlabel("Date", fontsize=9)
ax.set_yscale("log")
ax.set_ylabel("Cumulative return (log scale)", fontsize=9)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(OUTPUT_DIR/"figure_cumulative_excess_returns.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()
```

# Fama-French Three-Factor Regressions

## Regression Coefficients

```{python}
#| label: tbl-reg-build
#| include: false

def sig_star(t):
    a = abs(t)
    if a > 2.576: return "***"
    if a > 1.960: return "**"
    if a > 1.645: return "*"
    return ""

display_rows = []
for port in PORTFOLIO_COLS:
    r = reg_table.loc[port]
    display_rows.append({
        "Portfolio" : port,
        "α"         : f"{r['Alpha']:.4f}{sig_star(r['t(Alpha)'])}",
        "(t-α)"     : f"({r['t(Alpha)']:.2f})",
        "β MKT"     : f"{r['β(MKT)']:.4f}{sig_star(r['t(MKT)'])}",
        "(t-MKT)"   : f"({r['t(MKT)']:.2f})",
        "β SMB"     : f"{r['β(SMB)']:.4f}{sig_star(r['t(SMB)'])}",
        "(t-SMB)"   : f"({r['t(SMB)']:.2f})",
        "β HML"     : f"{r['β(HML)']:.4f}{sig_star(r['t(HML)'])}",
        "(t-HML)"   : f"({r['t(HML)']:.2f})",
        "R²"        : f"{r['R²']:.4f}",
        "N"         : f"{int(r['N']):,}",
    })

tbl = pd.DataFrame(display_rows).set_index("Portfolio")
```

```{python}
#| tbl-cap: "FF3 regression results. t-statistics in parentheses (Newey-West, 5 lags). *** p<0.01, ** p<0.05, * p<0.10."

```

## Alpha Estimates

```{python}
#| label: fig-alpha
#| fig-cap: "FF3 daily alpha estimates with ±2 SE error bars."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3.8

alphas  = reg_table["Alpha"]
t_stats = reg_table["t(Alpha)"]
se      = alphas / t_stats

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.8))
colors  = ["#2f6f73" if a >= 0 else "#a84c4c" for a in alphas]
ax.bar(alphas.index, alphas.values, color=colors, width=0.55, alpha=0.85)
ax.errorbar(alphas.index, alphas.values,
            yerr=2 * se.values,
            fmt="none", color="black", capsize=4, linewidth=1.1)
ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.9, linestyle="--")
ax.set_title("FF3 Alpha Estimates (± 2 SE)", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
ax.set_xlabel("Portfolio", fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylabel("Daily alpha (%)", fontsize=9)
ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=20)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(OUTPUT_DIR/"figure_alpha_bar.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()
```

# Interpretation

```{python}
#| label: tbl-interpretation

best_alpha = reg_table["Alpha"].abs().idxmax()
best_r2    = reg_table["R²"].idxmax()
mean_r2    = reg_table["R²"].mean()

findings = pd.DataFrame({
    "Finding"  : [
        "Average R²",
        "Highest |alpha|",
        "Best-fit portfolio",
        "SMB: Small vs Big LoBM",
        "HML: Small HiBM vs Big LoBM",
    ],
    "Value"    : [
        f"{mean_r2:.4f}",
        f"{best_alpha}  ({reg_table.loc[best_alpha,'Alpha']:.4f}% / day)",
        f"{best_r2}  (R² = {reg_table.loc[best_r2,'R²']:.4f})",
        f"{reg_table.loc['SMALL LoBM','β(SMB)']:.3f}  vs  "
        f"{reg_table.loc['BIG LoBM','β(SMB)']:.3f}",
        f"{reg_table.loc['SMALL HiBM','β(HML)']:.3f}  vs  "
        f"{reg_table.loc['BIG LoBM','β(HML)']:.3f}",
    ]
}).set_index("Finding")
display(findings)
```

**Market factor (MKT):** All portfolios load positively and significantly
near 1.0, consistent with well-diversified equity exposure.

**Size factor (SMB):** Small-cap portfolios carry large positive SMB loadings;
big-cap portfolios have near-zero or negative loadings — confirming size separation.

**Value factor (HML):** High-BM portfolios carry large positive HML loadings;
low-BM portfolios carry negative loadings — the classic value vs growth split.

**Alpha:** Most alphas are economically small and often statistically
indistinguishable from zero, confirming the FF3 model captures the bulk of
cross-sectional variation in these portfolios.

# References

- Fama, E. F., & French, K. R. (1993). Common risk factors in the returns on stocks and bonds. *Journal of Financial Economics*, 33(1), 3–56.
- French, K. R. Data Library. <https://mba.tuck.dartmouth.edu/pages/faculty/ken.french/data_library.html>
